previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, and watery diarrhea, initially concerning for gastroenteritis. Workup revealed no infectious cause, and symptoms improved with supportive care, antiemetics, and a short course of antibiotics. He had elevated liver enzymes with AST > ALT and right upper quadrant pain; imaging showed gallstones without cholecystitis. Given his history of amiodarone use, weight loss, and elevated inflammatory markers, autoimmune hepatitis and other chronic liver conditions were considered, but a liver biopsy was deferred due to anticoagulation. His INR was supratherapeutic, prompting temporary hold of warfarin, which was restarted at discharge. He was managed for multiple comorbidities including diastolic heart failure, diabetes, and COPD. He improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged in hepatology and rheumatology.

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ male with history of congestive heart
failure.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, most recently ___.

FINDINGS:  AP and lateral radiographs of the chest demonstrate clear lungs. 
There is a similar appearance to blunting of the bilateral CP angles probably
related to pleural parenchymal scar.  The heart remains enlarged.  The
mediastinal contours are unremarkable.  There is a two-lead implantable
cardiac defibrillator which is stable in appearance.  Median sternotomy wires
are again noted.  The pulmonary vasculature is remarkable for cephalization,
which appears chronic.

IMPRESSION:  Stable cardiomegaly and mild cephalization. There is no acute
chest pathology.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ male with coagulopathy and headache.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial images were acquired of the head without contrast and
reformatted in the coronal and sagittal planes.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of hemorrhage or recent infarction.  There is
no mass effect or extra-axial collection.  The ventricles and sulci are mildly
prominent consistent with age-appropriate atrophy.  Gray matter/white matter
differentiation is preserved.  There is bifrontal white matter hypodensity and
atrophy suggestion prior infarction or trauma.  There is atherosclerotic
calcification of the visualized portion of the carotid and vertebral arteries,
as well as ectasia of the right vertebral and basilar arteries.

The orbits and visualized soft tissues appear normal.  The visualized
paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.  Note is made of a high
riding left jugular bulb.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of hemorrhage or recent infarction. Chronic changes
as noted above.
